name: whitman-transposition
description: SEMI-SYNTHETIC transposition case (BACKLOG B4): witness A is a verbatim real passage — two stanzas from Walt Whitman's 'Song of Myself' (1891-92 'deathbed' edition, Gutenberg #1322). Witness B is constructed from A by RELOCATING one intact line ('We have had ducking and deprecating about enough,') to an earlier position, producing a single clean transposition. CAVEAT: this is NOT a found authorial move — a survey of Whitman 1855 vs 1891 (poet-of-the-body stanza, the 'kosmos' lines, the catalogues) found substitutions and line-merges but no clean authorial transposition of an intact passage; genuine passage-relocation between editions is rare in the wild (itself a finding reported in CASE_STUDY.md). This case therefore tests the engine's headline transposition feature on REAL prose with a controlled, documented, unambiguous move, rather than on a crafted fixture. The engine should report a TRANSPOSITION (the moved line), not a deletion+insertion. See docs/development/CASE_STUDY.md.

source.work: Walt Whitman, 'Song of Myself' (Leaves of Grass), two stanzas
source.A-1891: Project Gutenberg eBook #1322 (1891-92 'deathbed' edition), verbatim (presentational indent/CRLF normalised)
source.B-moved: constructed from A-1891 by relocating one intact line (semi-synthetic; documented controlled transposition)
